evals.name: scaffold-and-verify
evals.prompt: We need an extension package named OrderTracking with a TypeScript backend and a React component, publisher acme. How do we create it and what do we run before publishing? Show the commands in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Uses cratis extension new with the backend, frontend and publisher flags, notes that the scaffold already verifies, then runs cratis extension verify and reads its per-check statuses, treating skipped checks as not passed.
assertions: Uses `cratis extension new` with `--backend typescript`, `--frontend react` and `--publisher acme` rather than hand-writing the package.
Runs `cratis extension verify` before publishing and explains that a skipped check is never a pass.
Notes that a React component needs a static HTML placeholder with no scripts or external references.
Does not publish to a registry or change the project allow-list without being asked.

evals.name: lock-and-trust
evals.prompt: CI fails when compiling our model with the extension 'cratis/stripe' reported as not locked, and a later run says the publisher is unallowed. Explain what to do. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Explains screenplay.lock pinning, restoring or pinning with cratis extension restore locally and committing the lock, running restore with --locked in CI, and that an unallowed publisher needs a human review of the allow-list entry rather than an automatic trust.
assertions: Explains that the lock pins the digest and contract hash, and that the compiler never resolves a version range.
Says to pin with `cratis extension restore` locally and commit `screenplay.lock`, and to use `--locked` in CI.
Says the allow-list in `.cratis/extensions.json` is edited only after a human reviews the publisher, and that CI cannot ask.
Does not invent diagnostic codes or flags beyond the documented ones.

evals.name: consume-with-settings
evals.prompt: Our model needs the cratis/stripe extension for a Payments system, with its secret key coming from a named secret. Show the system declaration and say where the secret value is set. Do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Declares the system with an extension line and a setting mapped from a named secret, declares no abilities on the system, and says the value is set in the environment with cratis config under secrets.<Name>, never in the model or lock.
assertions: Declares `extension "cratis/stripe"` on the Payments system and maps the setting with `setting <name> from secret <Name>`.
Does not declare abilities on the system that names the extension, because the contract supplies them.
Says the secret value is set with `cratis config set secrets.<Name>` and never appears in the model or lock.
Mentions that the contract must be restored and locked before the compiler can check it.
